study.question: Does preserving field-specific relevance inside feedback-conditioned historical summaries improve joint field/history/task modeling beyond the same architecture using event-wide relevance and whole-history summaries?
study.hypothesis: The inspected DIN adaptation assigns one target-only weight to each concatenated exposure, includes historical action only in values, and supplies one summary to every task. This can average together category/brand/advertisement relevance and rare feedback evidence. A target/context-conditioned score for each item field, normalized within each of four overlapping host feedback masks plus an all-exposure group, may retain complementary evidence before joint static-field/summary/task interaction. This is a provisional mechanism, not an observed failure of DIN.

nearest_work.source_ref: paper:din; archived primary text content-sha256 5fee25f33f375e51b3ee9417d376ff9dbe2ea3628c932a7679ddfeb0feaaade2 lines 219-277
nearest_work.difference: Inherits field embeddings and target-conditioned retrieval concept. Uses normalized field-specific and feedback-conditioned summaries with explicit count features, rather than unnormalized local activation over concatenated events. This is not an exact DIN reproduction.

nearest_work.source_ref: unirank-code:HiFormer at 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines 113-159; paper:hiformer original text unavailable through registry
nearest_work.difference: Nearest stacked alternative: pooled history plus field/task tokens. Proposed difference is the field-by-feedback retrieval factorization before a small shared attention stack. Does not reproduce hierarchical low-rank heterogeneous HiFormer blocks. Original-method novelty remains unverified.

nearest_work.source_ref: unirank-code:EST at 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines 119-216; paper:est original text unavailable through registry
nearest_work.difference: Shares use of identifiable fields and sequence retrieval, but summarizes history once into five tokens and does not iteratively update event tokens or use EST per-token FFNs. No full-method superiority claim.

nearest_work.source_ref: unirank-code:TokenFormer at 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines 117-155; paper:tokenformer original text unavailable through registry
nearest_work.difference: Shares field/history/target interaction motivation; compresses the fixed visible history before interaction instead of retaining all events in full/sliding-window attention. Not a reproduction or verified original contribution.

inherited_components: Frozen four-label sample interface, released item/action embeddings (dimension 16), official_offline history and fixed host training recipe.
FeatureEmbeddingDict, MultiTaskModel input filtering, Dice tower activations and separate binary readouts from the existing adaptation.
Established target-aware pooling, field tokens, learned task queries, residual self-attention and feed-forward blocks as architectural concepts; new implementation does not copy benchmark model code.
study.proposed_difference: Replace DIN local activation and its single history summary with a representation study: six actual item fields are pooled using field-specific relevance within five groups (all visible exposures plus the four supplied feedback masks). Concatenate pooled field subvectors and an action subvector, project each group to width 32, add its log-count and identity, and jointly interact with separately projected static user/context/target fields and four task tokens through two small attention blocks. Query uses target field and mean user/context embeddings. No timestamps or current labels enter forward; target action is never read. All four variants include the same five count features, raw static skip path and summary/tower architecture. Event controls average field relevance logits before pooling; global controls replace group retrieval masks by whole-history masks but preserve actual counts and group absence flags. Thus factor comparisons isolate retrieval factorization, not the entire replacement relative to DIN. No positional modeling is claimed in this first study.
predictions: Primary predeclared comparison: field_feedback click AUC exceeds event_global on the full 2,871,767-sample validation. A gain over DIN alone does not identify either proposed factor.

Field factor: field_feedback-event_feedback and field_global-event_global have positive click AUC differences; feedback factor: field_feedback-field_global and event_feedback-event_global have positive differences. Report all four differences and the interaction (field_feedback-event_feedback)-(field_global-event_global), including negative values.
Secondary expectation: feedback grouping better preserves auxiliary-task AUC and unweighted logloss, but click AUC remains the selection criterion; do not substitute mean-task AUC.

Exploratory history-length diagnostics use existing empty/1-16/17-64/>64 bins with sample, positive and negative counts. Grouping should chiefly affect nonempty histories; empty-history differences can reflect training-mediated changes and are not direct retrieval effects. Baseline slice AUC differences are not causal evidence of dilution.

All four factorial variants must have exactly equal embedding and dense parameter counts. Measured training, inference throughput, p50/p95 whole-batch latency, peak memory, examples and allocated GPU seconds must be reported; similar dimensions do not establish equal wall time.
falsifiers: No advantage over event_global, or an advantage confined to DIN comparison, fails to support the combined field/feedback retrieval explanation.
If field-only or group-only replacements match or outperform the combined candidate, narrow or reject the interaction hypothesis; retain that simpler trajectory as a candidate.

If event controls match field-specific models at identical parameter counts, field-specific relevance is unsupported in this implementation. If global controls match grouped variants while counts remain available, separate feedback summaries are unsupported.

Nonfinite forward/backward results, sensitivity to masked field/action IDs, incorrect four-output shapes, nonzero summary from all-masked input, or access to current target action invalidates execution and requires correction before interpreting metrics.

A failed or timed-out implementation is an execution/resource outcome, not a refutation of the representation mechanism. A single seed is preliminary; a later paired repetition reversing gains weakens support.
alternative_explanations: Relative to DIN, normalized weights, explicit counts, static skip connections, context-conditioned retrieval, task tokens, shared interactions, parameter count and optimization all change. Only within-factorial contrasts attribute field or feedback retrieval effects.
Grouping introduces a useful inductive constraint and different effective rank even with identical trainable tensors. Equal nominal parameters do not equate optimization or functional capacity.

The shared event score is an additive aggregate of field logits, not a reproduction of DIN nonlinear concatenated-event attention. Results concern this controlled replacement, not every possible event encoder.
Group summaries overlap for composite action tokens; they are not independent behaviors. Rare auxiliary outcomes match user/category/brand within 24 hours and are not advertisement-level conversions.

Offline delayed feedback visibility, inherited whole-window filtering/vocabularies, time shift and single-pass optimization may affect any benefit. There is no established production point-in-time validity.

The mean context query and low-dimensional pooled group bottleneck may underfit; a negative result cannot exclude finer field-group tokens or iterative retrieval. No sequence-order dependency is represented.

The only committed trajectory is baseline-din: click AUC 0.6555440824200336, logloss 0.18339680255790589, 32,059,429 total/266,213 dense parameters, 328.9133 seconds wall, 4,196,814,848 peak GPU bytes. No failed, abandoned or competing local trajectories are supplied; external cards are not local successes.

contrasts.intervention: field_feedback full replacement versus DIN reference
contrasts.control: Committed baseline-din with matched frozen seed/data/recipe, plus event_global as closest new architecture control.
held_fixed: All visibility, labels, split, scoring and host optimizer/precision contracts
remaining_confounds: DIN versus replacement changes several components and dense parameter count; this comparison measures model performance, not mechanism attribution.
A committed reference is not a new paired seed; repeat candidate and closest control before repeated-support claims.
contrasts.decision_if_supported: Retain predictive improvement provisionally, inspect factorial attribution and measured quality/cost; do not label it novel or significant.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: Retain DIN and inspect all factorial outcomes, cost, rare-group sparsity and training stability before deciding whether a discriminating follow-up is warranted.

contrasts.intervention: 2x2 field_retrieval x feedback_groups, all four cells
held_fixed: Same source body except two architecture flags/defaults
Identical parameter tensors, module construction/initialization order and embedding dimensions
Same target/context query, action values, group counts/absence flags, static field tokens, two interaction blocks, task readouts and loss
Frozen full-data training recipe and primary validation score
remaining_confounds: Functional rank and inductive constraints change intentionally.
Runtime can differ across branches; report measured cost.
Single-seed comparison does not quantify initialization variability; no paired user-cluster bootstrap interface is currently exposed.
contrasts.decision_if_supported: Select using click AUC and retain only supported representation factors; reserve paired seeds and a later ordinary event-attention or capacity/cost control if the direction remains consequential.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: Prefer a supported simpler cell or DIN; record each null/negative trajectory and distinguish implementation failure from mechanism evidence. Do not tune on withheld results.

cost_plan.estimate_ref: run://r-001: baseline-din 328.9133 seconds wall; host estimated_unit_seconds 481.3476 and trial_cap_seconds 1203.3690. No torch exists in coding jail; preparation uses syntax/source checks only, and no training/calibration jobs are launched here. Host forward/backward/masking checks remain execution gates.
cost_plan.attribution_reserve: Four proposed full-data runs: planning estimate 4*481.3476=1925.3904 seconds, conservative cap sum 4*1203.3690=4813.4760 seconds. This is a budget estimate, not a measured cost for the new model. Reserve at least 12,000 additional seconds for failures, discriminating follow-ups and paired seeds of a selected cell/closest control. Count checks, diagnostics, retries, failures and preparation against the research clock.
cost_plan.assessment_reserve: Reserve at least 12,000 seconds for necessary repetitions, attribution and a validation-selected frozen final suite. This phase requests no held-out execution; no checkpoint exists for the proposed models. Freeze source/config/checkpoint hashes, selected candidates, controls, seeds and host commands before withheld assessment in an authorized later phase.
cost_plan.stop_rule: Preserve the fixed 172800-second wall-clock budget and host per-trial cap. Recompute remaining budget before execution; stop if no complete admissible study and required reserves fit, integrity fails or the user stops. No installation, local training, hidden-data inspection or budget increase. Four cells are screening-quality single-seed evidence until repetitions; do not declare success from budget exhaustion.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Pinned source inspected. Field identity and repeated retrieval are relevant, but current evidence does not justify the cost and attribution burden of per-layer event updates.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: Retain explicit field identity, but use one pooled representation stage with shared small attention blocks; no EST block is adopted.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No iterative event-state updates or feature-specific FFNs. Original primary method text unavailable, so novelty unverified.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If controlled field retrieval has no benefit, distinct field summaries are unsupported here.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: No local evidence yet for sequence dependency or hybrid sparse-attention savings at fixed length 100. The card is an external report, not a local result.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No HSTU transduction, sparse attention or length schedule.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Later controlled sequence-order diagnostics or measured cost could justify reconsideration.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: The available baseline contains no training-frequency evidence supporting expanded identifier embeddings. Keep the embedding budget fixed for this representation study.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Uniform dimension 16 and no dedicated expanded-ID path.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A later training-frequency-controlled comparison could demonstrate an ID-capacity limitation.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: No measured redundant-activation limitation or sparsity/runtime benefit supports competitive filtering in this initial contrast.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Small dense token interaction over compressed summaries.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Later matched dense-versus-sparse filtering could establish a useful activation-selection effect.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Nearest inspected stacked pooled-history/field/task-token architecture. Primary benchmark source establishes that these broad components are inherited concepts; original paper text not audited.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: Replace single history pooling by factorial field/feedback retrieval, use five compressed group tokens and ordinary shared two-layer attention.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No hierarchical low-rank token-specific HiFormer blocks. Candidate effect is defined relative to matched factorial replacements, not claimed as a new token framework.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If event_global matches field_feedback, the proposed retrieval difference is unsupported even if both beat DIN.
